# Expected values for the split of grain between the mill and the pig farm (docs/rules/grain-split.md, docs/rules/construction-materials.md),
# captured from the original program in the emulator (ADR 0008): tools/GhidraDump/emulate.py, the verb construct, which is remove with the
# phase routine 0x42965c at the last phase of each cycle (the castle's goods go out to the flags whose requests rank highest) and the
# player's default words 0x445752 and 0x44579c. Two finished buildings stand from the start: a pig farm (type 14, at the flag 15,9) and a
# mill (type 15, at the flag 18,6), both with their workers inside after the pass 362; the part castle-off@300 sets the castle's building
# type to 0 before the pass 300 (docs/rules/pig-farming.md, "The rank"); the click k@4,5 sets the castle's stock word of the grain (good 4)
# to 5 at the pass 700. Both ask for grain from the pass 362 on. The first four hand-outs, one per cycle (the passes 724, 757, 790, 823), go
# to the pig farm, the pig farm, the mill, and the pig farm; the lines run to the pass 899, where the original's castle hands nothing out
# at the pass 856 (its outstanding slots are full) and gives the fifth grain to the mill at the pass 889; the engine, which keeps no slots,
# hands the fifth out at 856 (docs/rules/construction-materials.md, "Stand-ins"), so the test checks only the passes before 856. The lines are the emulator's output reduced to what the engine
# reproduces: the items of the mill's flag (f2) and of the pig farm's flag (f3) (70 bytes, the request words at 0x42 to 0x45), the pig
# farm's item (b2) and the mill's (b3) (18 bytes: the status at 5, the fill bytes at 8 and 9; their flag pointers left out), the castle's
# grain and pig counts, and the generator. The flag and building slots are one higher than the engine's (the dummies of the tables).
# Not production code: no routine of the program is transcribed here, only values the program produced.
